messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: model load failures detected in pool eu-west-1a. 12/25 hosts reporting loader errors; ~30% request error rate. Paging on-call (maya)

maya: oncall here — seeing the page. what specifically is failing? any customer impact already visible?

jordan: quick summary from node logs — multiple hosts are failing during the model unmarshal step while loading weights. also seeing intermittent CUDA OOMs and a couple compile timeouts. stack traces attached below.

devon: logs from host gpu-17 (latest):
```
2026-03-14T09:45:02Z ERROR loader: UnmarshalError: tensor[0] shape mismatch (expected 3072, got 0) at model/weights.go:142
2026-03-14T09:45:03Z WARN  runtime: CudaError: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory (requested 134217728)
2026-03-14T09:45:05Z ERROR compile: OpKernel timeout after 30s while compiling attention_kern.cu
2026-03-14T09:45:06Z INFO  runtime: fallback triggered for model-bert-large-quant
```

jordan: looks like two failure modes: (1) deserialization/unmarshal producing zero-length tensors (possible corrupted checkpoint or broken streaming of weights), (2) subsequent memory pressure triggering cuMemAlloc failures and compile timeouts. some hosts recover after restart but others loop.

maya: impact? Are Hosted API customers failing, or only Dedicated?

jordan: Hosted endpoints with model pinned to this exact variant are returning 502s for ~30% of calls. Dedicated customers on reserved pools also seeing increased errors on the eu-west region; traffic is degrading but still partially serving via fallback variants on ~40% of requests.

helpdesk: flagging high-severity customer impact. preparing status page draft. suggested message: "We are investigating increased errors for text-generation in EU region; short term mitigation in progress." Need confirmation from SRE before publishing.

maya: mitigation plan proposed: (A) take affected hosts OOS to allow warmup to not retry and amplify errors, (B) flip routing policy to prefer smaller/quantized variant (model-bert-large-quant) for affected routes, (C) disable eager compile for new instances (temp config), (D) escalate to infra if multi-host OOM persists. any thumbs? :thumbsup:

devon: doing (A) now — cordoning gpu-17/gpu-19/gpu-21 and kicking drain; rolling restart attempt queued.

ops-bot: Command executed: `kubectl cordon gpu-17 && kubectl drain gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

jordan: (B) routing change applied to canary -> shifting 60% of new traffic to model-bert-large-quant for eu-west. fallback policy set to `route: prefer-quantized` in policy service.

maya: (C) how to disable eager compile? I can flip runtime flag but need approval — it reduces perf but avoids compile timeouts while we investigate.

sre-lead: approve. flip `RUNTIME_EAGER_COMPILE=false` for new nodes in pool eu-west-1a and restart warmup service. watch for regressions.

devon: applying env flip to warmup daemonset: `kubectl set env ds/warmup RUNTIME_EAGER_COMPILE=false -n redwood-serving`

ops-bot: Warmup daemonset updated. rolling restart started.

jordan: also noticed checksum mismatch warnings for the model shard stream on S3 mirror. requesting model-team to re-verify checkpoint integrity. pinging @model-team in infra.

maya: helpdesk — prepare a short status update: state what customers may see, mention region eu-west and that we’re routing to a quantized fallback. include ETA: investigating, mitigation in progress.

helpdesk: draft ready: "We are investigating intermittent errors for the text-generation API in Europe. We are routing traffic to a fallback model variant while we investigate; some customers may see slightly different outputs. No data loss. We’ll update within 1 hour." Any edits?

maya: looks good. publish when Jordan confirms fallback stable for 10 minutes.

jordan: fallback stable for 8 minutes, error rate dropped from 30% to ~6% on canary traffic. still seeing a handful of nodes fail after restart with the same UnmarshalError.

devon: note: when a node hits UnmarshalError it often leaves partial artifacts in /var/lib/redwood/cache — I'll add cleanup step to the drain script to avoid repeated fails on restart.

maya: good call. add `rm -rf /var/lib/redwood/cache/model-bert-large-*` to prestop hook for now.

ops-bot: Prestop updated in daemonset.

jordan: model-team update: S3 checksums show two shards with inconsistent sizes uploaded on 2026-03-12 02:14 UTC. Rolling reupload scheduled; rehashing in progress. If deserialization is due to corrupted shards, reupload should fix. Meanwhile we keep routing to quantized fallback and avoid warmup of the full model.

sre-lead: taking over incident for next shift. I'll coordinate infra and model-team. plan: (1) keep fallback routing until reupload done (2) mark affected hosts OOS until drain/cleanup passes (3) run full-model load tests on a canary host with the reuploaded shards when available (4) if reupload not completed in 45m, escalate to exec for customer communication.

maya: handing off to sre-lead. oncall signing off, will monitor from mobile.

sre-lead: noted. if anyone sees new CUDA OOM counts spike >5/min across pool, alert me immediately. I will post updates here.

helpdesk: status page published. ticket created: INC-2026-3298 with affected customer list attached.

incident-bot: Incident assigned to sre-lead; escalation timer set 45m.

sre-lead: starting coordination with infra/model-team; I expect a follow-up within 20m. will attach postmortem checklist once stabilized.

ops-bot: Handoff acknowledgement recorded by oncall-bot.

sre-lead: taking the channel private for sensitive logs; continuing in #incidents-private-1982100000 if needed. end of handoff for now.
